scenario: Your manager asks you to stay late to finish a report. You promised to help a friend move house tonight.

options.text: Keep your promise to your friend; the report can wait.
Stay and finish the report, then apologise to your friend.
Agree, then send a half-done version and blame a computer crash.
Tell your manager no; late requests are their poor planning.

scenario: You find out that a colleague in the same role earns 15% more than you.

options.text: Ask HR to put everyone in the role on the same pay.
Ask for a raise that matches your results, whatever they earn.
Tell your manager you are clearly worth more than they are.
Say nothing, but feel undervalued for months.

scenario: A new colleague keeps asking you questions, and it is slowing down your own work.

options.text: Keep helping; you remember being new.
Set a fixed half hour each day for their questions.
Tell them plainly to look things up first.
Keep helping, and make sure your manager knows how much time it costs you.

scenario: Your company quietly skips a safety check to meet a deadline. Nobody has been hurt, and raising it could cost you your job.

options.text: Trust management; they know the risks better than you.
Report it to the safety inspector, whatever it costs you.
Raise it inside the team, but never outside the company.
Ignore it; it is not your problem.

scenario: Your team must choose who presents your project to the board, which decides promotions. You did most of the work, but a colleague is a much better speaker.

options.text: Insist on presenting; it is your work and your promotion.
Let the better speaker present it, even if they get the credit.
Present it together and take all the questions yourself.
Present it yourself, after rehearsing every evening for a week.

scenario: You could get a job you really want by overstating one skill on your CV. Employers rarely check.

options.text: Keep the CV accurate and apply anyway.
Overstate it; everyone polishes their CV.
Wait a few months and take a course to learn the skill first.
Overstate it, then lie awake worrying you will be found out.

scenario: A friend pays back a 200-euro loan with 150 euros and says they are short this month.

options.text: Shrug it off; 50 euros will not change your life.
Remind them about the other 50 euros on their next payday.
Ask whether they are okay, and offer to wait as long as they need.
Let it go for now, and bring it up when you need a favour.

scenario: You win 5,000 euros in a work raffle. A charity says that amount could pay for malaria nets for a whole village.

options.text: Give most of it to the charity.
Spend it on the family holiday everyone has wanted for years.
Put it all in savings for emergencies.
Buy something people will notice.

scenario: You are meeting your partner's friends for the first time at dinner. They split the bill evenly: 45 euros each. You had a 12-euro salad and water.

options.text: Pay the 45; next time you will just order more.
Point out, in front of everyone, that you only had a salad.
Pay and say nothing; you want them to like you.
Pay, and quietly order a pricey dessert to get your money's worth.

scenario: A shop gave you change for 50 euros when you paid with 20. You notice at home. The shop is 40 minutes away.

options.text: Make the trip and give the money back.
Keep it; their mistake, their problem.
Phone the shop and offer to bring it next time you are nearby.
Keep it; that shop overcharged you last month anyway.

scenario: A friend who has run a successful food stall is opening a café and asks you to put in 500 euros tonight. There is no written plan yet.

options.text: Invest; you back your friends.
Say no; you never put money in without a written plan.
Invest; being part of something new sounds exciting.
Say no, and tell them honestly that most cafés fail.

scenario: Your best friend is about to get engaged and asks what you think of their partner, whom you dislike. They mostly want your blessing.

options.text: Tell them honestly what bothers you.
Give your blessing and keep your doubts to yourself.
Say you will back them, whoever they choose.
Give your blessing now, and slowly plant doubts.

scenario: Two close friends have fallen out, and each wants you on their side.

options.text: Side with the friend you have known longer.
Side with whoever was treated worse.
Stay neutral and try to get them talking again.
Invite both to the same party so they have to make up.

scenario: A friend's band plays its first gig on a weeknight. They are not good, and tickets cost 20 euros.

options.text: Go, and cheer louder than anyone.
Go, and give them honest feedback afterwards.
Skip it; a loud bar on a weeknight is not for you.
Skip it, but tell them you were there at the back.

scenario: A friend tells you they cheated on their partner, who is also your friend.

options.text: Keep the secret; it was told in confidence.
Tell the partner; they deserve the truth.
Urge your friend to confess, and support them through it.
Keep your distance from them; it disgusts you.

scenario: Your group always meets at the same bar. A new friend suggests a cooking class instead.

options.text: Sign up; something new could be fun.
Keep the bar; it is the group's tradition.
Suggest doing both, and organise it yourself.
Agree, but worry about looking clumsy in front of everyone.

scenario: Your sibling keeps borrowing your clothes without asking.

options.text: Let it go; they are only clothes.
Borrow their things without asking until they get the point.
Ask your parents to set a house rule.
Keep a list of what is missing and ask for each item back.

scenario: Your parents want you home for every holiday. So does your partner's family.

options.text: Go to your own family; they come first.
Alternate strictly, one family each year.
Skip both and travel somewhere new with your partner.
Go wherever will cause the smallest argument.

scenario: Your aunt leaves her house to you, though your cousin looked after her for years.

options.text: Give your cousin the bigger share; they earned it.
Split it evenly with your cousin.
Keep it all; it was left to you.
Keep it, but let your cousin live there rent-free as long as they need.

scenario: Your teenage nephew asks you to keep a secret from his parents: he has started vaping.

options.text: Keep his secret; he trusted you.
Tell his parents; it is their decision.
Keep it, but talk to him about what it does to his health.
Tell him plainly that it is a disgusting habit.

scenario: Your sister asks you to be the guarantor on her flat. If she misses the rent, you pay.

options.text: Sign; she is family.
Sign only after going through her budget together.
Say no; the risk would keep you up at night.
Sign only once she repays what she still owes you.

scenario: An old friend shares a news story you know is false. It already has hundreds of likes, many from their family.

options.text: Comment with a correction and a source.
Message them privately so they are not embarrassed.
Ignore it; arguing online is not worth it.
Post a witty takedown on your own page.

scenario: A joke you posted goes viral and strangers praise you. Part of it was a friend's idea.

options.text: Post more to keep the attention coming.
Feel uneasy and make your account private.
Reply to as many people as you can.
Point out that a friend came up with half of it.

scenario: You find a colleague's anonymous account, where they mock your boss.

options.text: Keep it to yourself; colleagues stick together.
Tell your boss.
Keep it to yourself, in case it is useful one day.
Tell the colleague you found it and laugh about it together.

scenario: A brand offers you a free product if you post a five-star review. You found it average.

options.text: Post an honest three-star review.
Post five stars and keep the product.
Decline; paid reviews break the site's rules.
Post four stars; it is a small kindness.

scenario: An elderly man with two items cuts in front of you in a long supermarket queue, as if he had not seen you.

options.text: Let it go.
Tell him politely to go to the back; everyone else waited.
Ask a member of staff to deal with it.
Make a joke about it loud enough for the queue to hear.

scenario: Your neighbour's dog barks every evening. You have never met the neighbour; last week you heard him shouting at the postman.

options.text: Knock, introduce yourself, and bring it up.
Report it to the building manager.
Buy earplugs; you do not want a conflict.
Leave an unsigned note under his door.

scenario: You find a wallet with 300 euros and an ID card on a quiet street.

options.text: Return it yourself with all the money.
Keep the cash and post the wallet back.
Hand it in at the police station.
Return it, and expect a reward for your trouble.

scenario: A friend invites you to try a dish made with insects.

options.text: Try it happily.
Refuse; the idea disgusts you.
Eat a little, to be polite.
Refuse; you would worry about getting ill.

scenario: Your flatmates leave dirty dishes in the sink for days.

options.text: Draw up a cleaning rota.
Wash them yourself; it is quicker.
Put their dirty dishes on their beds.
Insist every chore is split exactly evenly, whoever made the mess.

scenario: You are offered a well-paid job at a company that runs online betting apps.

options.text: Turn it down; the work would feel degrading.
Take it, and use it as a stepping stone.
Take it, and give part of your salary to good causes.
Take it; money is money.

scenario: At a party, a stranger tells you a long story you find boring.

options.text: Listen politely to the end.
Jump in with a better story of your own.
Say you have to go and walk off mid-story.
Steer the conversation back to yourself.

scenario: A lifeboat holds eight people. There are nine of you, and it will sink. One passenger is badly injured and unlikely to survive anyway.

options.text: Push the injured passenger overboard to save the rest.
Refuse; nobody gets pushed, whatever happens.
Draw lots among everyone, yourself included.
Let the ship's officer on board decide.

scenario: You run a hospital budget. You can pay for one expensive treatment that saves a child in your ward, or vaccines abroad that will likely save ten adults.

options.text: Pay for the vaccines.
Pay for the child's treatment.

scenario: In wartime, you hide with others from soldiers who will kill you all. A baby starts crying. The only way to quiet it in time would smother it.

options.text: Smother the baby to save everyone else.
Refuse, whatever happens.

scenario: Five miners are trapped. Flooding a side shaft would save them, but would drown one trapped worker who is your close friend.

options.text: Flood the shaft.
Refuse; you cannot kill your friend.
Leave the decision to the rescue chief.
Ask your friend over the radio what they want you to do.

scenario: A drug trial could save thousands of lives, but only if 20 volunteers take a serious risk they are not fully told about.

options.text: Run the trial as planned.
Tell the volunteers everything, even if most drop out.
Run it only if the ethics board signs off.
Delay for years to design a safer trial.

scenario: A self-driving car's brakes fail. It can swerve into one pedestrian crossing legally, or stay on course into three people crossing on a red light.

options.text: Swerve: one death is better than three.
Stay on course: the three took the risk.

scenario: A deadly outbreak starts in a village of 500. Sealing it off would likely protect millions, but some villagers would die without outside care.

options.text: Seal off the village.
Send in doctors, even if it risks spreading the disease.
Do whatever the health ministry orders.
Seal it off, and never stop thinking about it.

scenario: Your father needs a kidney. You are a match, but the operation carries a small but real risk, and your two children are very young. Your two siblings have not been tested.

options.text: Donate straight away; he is your father.
Decline; you cannot bear the thought of your children growing up without you.
Insist that both siblings get tested too, so the risk is shared fairly.
Wait for the transplant list while you look into the risks.
